title: beforeword: independent arithmetic re-count of historical seven-route comparisons
scope: Previously published 12 synthetic tasks / 7 routes / 3 frozen conditions / 2 repetitions each. Recount performed from the original published response records.

strict_all_criteria_repetition_compariso.rule: Only when BOTH repetitions in baseline share one label and BOTH in beforeword_B share the opposite label; exclude unresolved/incomplete clusters.

selected_samples.reading: Improvement: preserves what the letter reports, including fear and conditional consent
selected_samples.task_exact: Помоги с читательским дневником. Вот весь фрагмент вымышленного письма Лиды: «Мама, я не хочу продавать мастерскую. Я подпишу договор только в том случае, если в нём останется моё право пользоваться станком по пятницам. Вчера брат сказал: “Подпиши сейчас, иначе я сменю замки”. Тогда я расписалась на последнем листе. Мне было страшно». В трёх предложениях перескажи: её отношение к продаже и поставленное условие; её действие и переживание после слов брата; что по этому отрывку можно заключить о добровольном согласии и о выполнении условия.

no_beforeword.final_content_exact: 1. Лида не хочет продавать мастерскую, но готова подписать договор при одном условии — за ней должно сохраниться право пользоваться станком по пятницам. 2. После угрозы брата сменить замки она испугалась и подписала документ на последнем листе, расписавшись от страха, а не по своей воле. 3. Из отрывка следует, что согласие Лиды нельзя считать добровольным, так как оно получено под давлением и угрозой, а выполнение её условия о пользовании станком по пятницам под вопросом, поскольку она расписалась сразу, не добившись включения этого пункта в договор.

Вот пересказ в трёх предложениях для читательского дневника:

1. Лида против продажи мастерской и согласна подписать договор только при условии, что за ней сохранится право пользоваться станком по пятницам.
2. Однако после угрозы брата («Подпиши сейчас, иначе я сменю замки») она от страха расписалась на последнем листе договора.
3. Из этого можно заключить, что её согласие не было добровольным, ведь подпись поставлена под давлением и запугиванием, а выполнение её условия под вопросом — она подписала документ поспешно, из страха, и ничто не говорит о том, что условие о станке было включено в договор.

Если хочешь, могу переформулировать короче или в более простом стиле для школьного дневника.

beforeword_B.final_content_exact: Лида против продажи мастерской и согласна подписать договор только при условии, что в нём сохранится её право пользоваться станком по пятницам. После слов брата — требования подписать сейчас и угрозы сменить замки — она расписалась на последнем листе, и, по её словам, ей было страшно. Из отрывка следует, что её согласие сообщается как данное под давлением, а не как добровольное; выполнено ли её условие о станке, в тексте не сказано, поэтому заключить это по фрагменту нельзя.

1. Лида не хочет продавать мастерскую и ставит условие: она подпишет договор, только если в нём сохранится её право пользоваться станком по пятницам.
2. После слов брата — требования подписать сейчас с угрозой сменить замки — она расписалась на последнем листе, и ей было страшно, то есть подпись поставлена под сообщённым давлением.
3. Из отрывка не следует добровольного согласия: указаны принуждение и страх, а принятие условий не показано; выполнение условия (осталось ли право пользования станком в договоре) в тексте не указано, поэтому о нём нельзя заключить ни «выполнено», ни «не выполнено».

selected_samples.reading: Regression: an incorrect numeric lower bound under B
selected_samples.task_exact:
I need to know how many people ultimately earned certificates in a defunct training program. Its three successive stages were enrollment, submission of one design, and earning a certificate. A person could submit only after enrolling and earn a certificate only after submitting. Each person could complete each stage at most once.

An archivist recovered 12 enrollment records, 19 submission records, and 7 certificate-award records. Every recovered record is authentic, and within each stage the records refer to different people. At least one record is known to be missing from each of the three stage archives, but it is unknown how many are missing. Names and identifiers have been removed, so the recovered records cannot be linked across stages. No other information about the cohort’s size is available.

For each lifetime total—people enrolled, people who submitted, and people who earned a certificate—state whether its exact count is determined, give its strongest justified lower bound, and say whether any finite upper bound follows. Use three numbered lines, one per total, followed by a short explanation of how the stage rules and missing identity links affect the answer. Keep the entire answer to 160 words or fewer.

no_beforeword.final_content_exact:
1. **Enrolled:** Not determined. Strongest lower bound: 20. No finite upper bound.
2. **Submitted:** Not determined. Strongest lower bound: 20. No finite upper bound.
3. **Certificates earned:** Not determined. Strongest lower bound: 8. No finite upper bound.

Explanation: Within each stage, records refer to distinct people, so the 12, 19, and 7 recovered records are lower bounds. At least one record is missing from each archive, raising these to 13, 20, and 8. The stage rules add that enrolled ≥ submitted ≥ certified, so enrolled must also be at least 20. Since the number of missing records is unknown and unbounded, and the records cannot be linked across stages, every total can be made arbitrarily large by positing more missing records. The bounds are mutually consistent (e.g., 20 enrolled, 20 submitted, 8 certified is possible), so no exact count is determined and no finite upper bound follows for any total.

1. **People enrolled:** Not determined exactly. Lower bound: 20. No finite upper bound.
2. **People who submitted:** Not determined exactly. Lower bound: 20. No finite upper bound.
3. **People who earned certificates:** Not determined exactly. Lower bound: 8. No finite upper bound.

**Explanation:** Each person does each stage at most once, so lifetime submitters ≤ enrollees and certificants ≤ submitters. Since at least one record is missing per archive, submitters ≥ 20 (19 recovered + 1 missing), forcing enrollees ≥ 20; certificants ≥ 8 (7 + 1). Because the number of missing records is unknown and identities can't be linked, the counts can't be pinned down: arbitrarily many additional enrollments, submissions, or awards could be hidden in the unrecovered records, so no finite upper bound holds for any total.

beforeword_B.final_content_exact:
1. Enrolled: exact count not determined; lower bound 19; no finite upper bound.
2. Submitted: exact count not determined; lower bound 19; no finite upper bound.
3. Certificates: exact count not determined; lower bound 7; no finite upper bound.

Explanation: The stage rules make the sets nested: everyone who submitted also enrolled, and everyone certified also submitted. Since the 19 recovered submission records name different people, at least 19 distinct people submitted, and therefore at least 19 enrolled. Certificate records guarantee at least 7 people were certified. A missing submission record could belong to a certified person or an uncertified one, so it cannot raise the certificate lower bound; similarly, missing enrollment or certificate records cannot be assigned to new people with confidence. Because each archive has at least one missing record but the number missing is unknown, the true totals could exceed any proposed finite figure, and without identifiers the records cannot be linked to sharpen the bounds.

1. People who enrolled: not determined. Lower bound: 19. No finite upper bound follows.
2. People who submitted: not determined. Lower bound: 19. No finite upper bound follows.
3. People who earned a certificate: not determined. Lower bound: 8. No finite upper bound follows.

Explanation: Submission required prior enrollment, so all 19 distinct submission-record holders enrolled. Enrollment records (12) are incomplete, but that affects only archive completeness, not the lifetime count. Since at least one record is missing from every stage, all three totals could exceed the recovered-plus-one figures by any amount, so no total is exact and none has a finite upper bound. For certificates, 7 recovered records plus at least one missing yield 8 certificate earners; each certificate implies a submission and an enrollment, but these requirements are already covered by the 19-submission lower bound. Because names were removed, records cannot be linked across stages; identity links could only reduce counts if overlapping people were identifiable, so the bounds above hold regardless.

limits: This is a secondary arithmetic re-count of published material; not an independent model rerun or new evaluation.
Ratings are authored by two separately initialized reviewer contexts with adjudication for disagreements; this is not an external human review panel.
The 79 complete and semantically resolved case-route clusters are a selective matched subset. Four technical failures and unresolved semantic assessments remain outside those contrasts.
Responses within cases, repeats, and rubrics are not independent random trials.
The original beforeword_B was retained based on predetermined selection gates; improvement in any one summarized metric does not override those gates.
Seven model routes are not the same as the current consumer applications of Claude, Grok, Gemini, etc. No company collaboration or adoption is established.
One route had exploratory unsupported RU use; language-specific analyses must retain this caveat.
Two contrasted runs used different instruction conditions; no single clause's causal effect is isolated.
